questions.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror such that the image of the object is of the same size as the object?

options.text: Between curvature C and focus F
Between focus F and pole P

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Center of curvature at C.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **To get an image of the same size as the object in a concave mirror, the object should be placed at the centre of curvature of the mirror.**
 
• **Centre of curvature:-**
 
 
• **It is the point on the mirror that is the same distance from all points on the mirror's surface.**
 
• When an object is placed at the centre of curvature, the light rays from the object are reflected back so that they converge at the same point on the other side of the mirror.
 
• **This point is where the image is formed. The image is real, inverted, and the same size as the object.**

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:** 

 
 
• This is the **vascular tissue** in **plants** that conducts water and dissolved nutrients upward from the root and also helps to form the woody element in the stem. 
 
• The main function of **xylem **is to **transport water,** but it also transports some nutrients through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• This is the most common type of **plant tissue **found in the **soft parts of plants.**
 
• It is responsible for the **plant's metabolic functions, such as photosynthesis, storage of starch, fats and oils, and helps in the healing and repair of wounds.**
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• This tissue gives support to the plant and is usually found in** layers beneath the epidermis**.
 
• **Collenchyma cells** are elongated cells with thickened cell walls that provide structure and **support for the plant, particularly in regions of new growth**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• This is the** living tissue** that transports the** soluble organic compounds made during photosynthesis and known as photosynthates, in particular, sugar, from leaves to the rest of the plant where needed.**
 
• This process is called **translocation**.

questions.question: When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called **impulsive force.__**
 
• Impulse = force x time = change in momentum
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity.
 
• SI Unit of Impulse is Newton second (Ns).

__**Explanation:**__

Impulse

 
• When a large force works on a body for a very small time interval, it is called impulsive force.
 
• An impulsive force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.
 
• The impulse caused by a force during a specific time interval is equal to the body's change of momentum during that time interval.
 
• Impulse, effectively, is a measure of change in momentum.
 
• The impulse of a force is a measure of the total effect of force.
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity and its direction is the same as that of force.
 
• SI unit of impulse is Newton-second or kg-m-s-1 and CGS unit is g.m/s

questions.question: During photosynthesis the oxygen in glucose comes from ______.

options.text: Both from water and carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis is the physiochemical process, in which carbohydrates (organic compounds) are formed from inorganic substrates like H₂O & CO₂ in the presence of light and pigments.
 
• O₂ is evolved as a by-product during photosynthesis.
 
• The **oxygen molecule present in glucose is derived from carbon dioxide** during **Calvin cycle of photosynthesis**.
 
• The CO₂ molecule is first added to 3-phosphoglycerate during the carboxylation reaction of Calvin cycle, and is later used to form glucose.
 
• While molecular oxygen that is liberated during photosynthesis is produced from photolysis of water during the light reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis can be simply divided into 4 major processes

 
• Absorption of light energy by **Chlorophyll pigment.**
 
• Conversion of light energy into chemical energy.
 
• **Splitting of water or Photolysis** during Non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

** H₂O → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻⁻ + [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/utkar/AppData/Local/Temp/OICE_7537A668-6D1D-4E05-8EA6-84C3B2569657.0/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image004.png] O₂ **↑

**The oxygen that evolved during this process comes from water__**.

 
• **Reduction of CO₂ to carbohydrates (Glucose) during Dark reaction.**

**​**The CO2 undergoes reduction and its O2 is utilized in the formation of Glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

The **O₂ released during photolysis is the evolved O₂**, whereas **the O₂ released during the reduction of CO₂ is the O₂ in glucose.**

questions.question: Which isotope is used in the treatment of goitre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Iodine 131__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A goitre is a lump or swelling at the front of the neck caused by a **swollen thyroid**.
 
• Goitre is an adaptive reaction of the cells in your thyroid to any process that **blocks thyroid hormone production**.
 
• The most common cause of goiter worldwide is **iodine deficiency**.
 
• It is treatable.
 
• **Iodine-131** is a radioactive isotope used in the treatment of goitre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Uranium-235** is used for **nuclear fission and the production of electricity**.

questions.question: Identify an example of organisms that are free-swimming and bottom-dwelling forms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zooplankton**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**Zooplankton:

__
 
• Zooplankton is the common name given to many small species of animals found in fresh and marine waters throughout the world.
 
• The word zooplankton, derived from Greek, means "wandering animals."
 
• They float in the water column and drift with the currents. Most of these animals are so minute they are visible only with a microscope, although some species can reach lengths of eight feet.
 
• Two general groups of zooplankton exist those that remain planktonic throughout their entire life (holoplankton), and those that are larval stages of larger life forms (meroplankton).
 
• Some examples of zooplankton are Krill, jellyfish, Portuguese man o' war, squid, etc. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

Phytoplanktons:

 
• Derived from the Greek words phyto (plant) and plankton (made to wander or drift), phytoplankton are microscopic organisms that live in watery environments, both salty and fresh. 
 
• Some phytoplankton are bacteria, some are protists, and most are single-celled plants.
 
• Among the common kinds are cyanobacteria, silica-encased diatoms, dinoflagellates, green algae, and chalk-coated coccolithophores.

questions.question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the only organelles found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
 
• They are responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• In prokaryotic cells, ribosomes are smaller (70S) compared to those in eukaryotic cells (80S).
 
• Despite the size difference, the fundamental function of ribosomes remains the same across both cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic cells** do not have membrane-bound organelles, which distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** contain various membrane-bound organelles, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes, which are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The presence of ribosomes in both cell types highlights their essential role in the fundamental process of protein synthesis.
 
• The differences in ribosome size between prokaryotes and eukaryotes are due to variations in their ribosomal RNA and protein content.

questions.question: The major excretory product in human beings is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Urea.**__

__
 
• When our cells perform their functions, certain **waste products** are released. These are toxic and hence need to be **removed** from the body.
 
• The process of **removal of wastes** produced in the cells of the living organisms is called **excretion**. The parts involved in excretion from the excretory system.
 
• **Human excretory system:** A mechanism to filter the blood is required and done by the blood capillaries in the **kidneys**. When the blood reaches the two kidneys, it contains both **useful **and **harmful** substances. The **useful substances are absorbed back** into the blood. The wastes dissolved in water are removed as **urine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e41f1740cdb8115a19d9bbfcf5e898af70219f2d79922d8483412abbbc330bb3.png] 

 
• **Aquatic animals** like **fishes**, excrete cell waste as **ammonia** which directly dissolves in water.
 
• The major excretory product in **humans is urea**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• An adult human being normally passes about 1–1.8 L of urine in 24 hours. The urine consists of 95% water, 2.5% urea, and 2.5% other waste products.

questions.question: An echo returned in 2s. What is the distance of the reflecting surface from the source, given that the speed of the sound is 342 ms⁻¹.
questions.solution:
Speed of sound = 342 m/s.

Time taken for hearing an echo = 2s.

Distance travelled = 2d = v × t

2 × d = 342 × 2

d = (342 × 2)/2

= **342 m**
